newsitem.title: USA: District of Columbia agencies told to close gap.
newsitem.headline: District of Columbia agencies told to close gap.

text.p: The chief financial officer of the District of Columbia on Thursday said he was requiring agency heads to find savings to close an $85.4 million budget gap in fiscal 1997.

"By asking agency heads to identify ways to address the budget gap, we will provide the flexiblity necessary to uphold the budget priorities established in the fiscal year 1997 plan and budget," said Williams, in prepared remarks.

In a memo issued this week, Anthony Williams, along with the City Administrator, Michael Rogers, set individual budget targets for the agencies and required a detailed plan be submitted to the budget office by January 16.

While the Financial Authority has specified some program cuts, agency heads mostly are free to meet the savings goals "by whatever means best sustains service delivery priorities and provides structural change," the officials wrote, ruling out non-permanent reductions.

They noted the District is required to cut 1,090 full-time equivalent workers by March 1, 1997, with another 1,321 of reductions for planning purposes mandated by year-end. The second wave of reductions will require "extensive privatization," Williams and Rogers said.
Further, all the cost-saving steps must be realized in 1997, the officials stressed, adding the structural nature of the changes should produce further savings in future fiscal years.
